import time
from collections import OrderedDict


class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, maxsize):
        if maxsize < 1:
            raise ValueError("maxsize must be >= 1")
        self.maxsize = maxsize
        self._data = OrderedDict()  # key -> (value, expires_at or None)

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        item = self._data.get(key)
        if item is None:
            return default
        value, expires_at = item
        if expires_at is not None and time.monotonic() >= expires_at:
            del self._data[key]
            return default
        self._data.move_to_end(key)
        return value

    def put(self, key, value, ttl=None):
        """ttl is in seconds; None means the entry never expires."""
        expires_at = None if ttl is None else time.monotonic() + ttl
        self._data[key] = (value, expires_at)
        self._data.move_to_end(key)
        # ponytail: expiry is lazy (checked on get), so a dead entry holds a slot
        # until read or LRU-evicted. Add an expiry heap if that wastes real capacity.
        if len(self._data) > self.maxsize:
            self._data.popitem(last=False)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self._data)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    assert c.get("a") == 1          # a is now most recent
    c.put("c", 3)                   # evicts b
    assert c.get("b") is None and c.get("a") == 1 and c.get("c") == 3
    c.put("a", 10)                  # overwrite, no growth
    assert c.get("a") == 10 and len(c) == 2

    c.put("t", "x", ttl=0.05)       # evicts c
    assert c.get("t") == "x"
    time.sleep(0.06)
    assert c.get("t", "gone") == "gone" and len(c) == 1

    c.put("n", None)                # stored None is not a miss-with-crash
    assert c.get("n", "default") is None

    try:
        LRUCache(0)
        raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")
    except ValueError:
        pass
    print("ok")
